items.title: [负面] The direction the developers have taken with this...
items.summary:
The direction the developers have taken with this game recently has been nothing short of disappointing. Under the pretense of "reworking" the endgame, they have actively made it worse. They resorted to one of the most despised forms of balancing in a PvE game: instead of making any meaningful mechanical adjustments, they simply inflated enemy stats and called it a day.

Content that was supposed to have a gradual, stair-step progression curve now has enemy scaling amplified by factors of five or even ten between stages. The result is that even players with endgame-level builds cannot clear the final stages, while newer players run straight into a wall just trying to move from the first step to the second. And, of course, they decided to lock essential progression resources behind that wall.

Then, under the label of a "bug fix," they suddenly wiped out nearly 16% of one character's performance after that behavior had remained in the game for almost a year. They offered no meaningful explanation afterward and took no follow-up action. They seem to have forgotten that this is a gacha game. Calling something a "bug fix" is not a blank check that lets you suddenly nerf a character's long-established performance after players have already made decisions about investing in that character.

What makes all of this even more absurd is that these are the things they chose to spend their time doing while ignoring the feedback players have consistently given them in the hope of making the game better. Players have repeatedly asked for unique illustrations for character cards. They have repeatedly asked for more skins for characters. Every time, the developers' answer was essentially:

"Those things require roughly the same amount of resources as developing an entirely new character, so realistically, they are difficult to implement. Instead, we will quickly provide other ways for players to show their dedication to the characters they love."

When they added an extra passive to the final upgrade tier of characters—something that had previously been completely unnecessary—they fed us the same kind of reassuring line:

"This is meant to reward players who have poured their love into these characters. We will never allow power inflation to be balanced around characters at their maximum upgrade tier."

And players accepted that. So what did those players get in return?

Unannounced character nerfs. Power inflation so extreme that even bringing a full lineup of maxed-out characters is no longer enough. Ham-fisted mechanics whose entire design philosophy seems to be: "Don't play cards!" "Don't attack enemies!" "Don't even gain shields!", "We scaled HP up by more than 10x but anyway—Don’t fight prolonged!”. New-player progression has been crippled because the progression curve itself has collapsed, creating massive barriers for anyone trying to get into the game. And after all the talk about "rewarding players who love their characters," what do we get? Barely noticeable card borders that require a ridiculous amount of pointless effort to unlock.

This does not even look like simple greed. If money were the goal, they could at least use some kind of carrot-and-stick approach to tempt players into thinking, "Maybe if I invest just a little more, I can clear this." Instead, their recent decisions feel completely one-dimensional, with no apparent plan for what the consequences are supposed to be.

It's not as though this game has never made mistakes before. It has, plenty of times. And players were willing to give them the benefit of the doubt. "They make a lot of mistakes, but those mistakes come from caring about the game." That was the excuse people were willing to accept. But at this point, their decision-making has reached a singularity; it could no longer distinguish from malice.

I'm not writing such a harsh review just to dismiss this game as garbage. I love this game, and I have seen countless times how much the developers themselves care about it. That is exactly why it is so painful—and so difficult to understand—to watch the game fall apart in such an unreasonable way through their recent decisions.

What players want now is not merely damage control for the current situation. We want a commitment to make sure this never happens again. The developers spent a long time building trust with their players. But that trust has gradually been spent, mistake after incomprehensible mistake, until now there is virtually none left.

I hope they understand that the love and trust players have for this game are not infinite.

items.title: [负面] I mostly play on mobile but wanted to express my d...
items.summary: I mostly play on mobile but wanted to express my discontent more publicly so I reviewed here as well. I had previously reviewed this game positively, but as it stands now, 3 months after I started, the devs have consistently made baffling decisions that leave the game in an objectively worse state than it was 3 months ago. They've completely butchered the most enjoyable endgame mode and made many people not even want to touch it. They previously PROMISED that when they added new power levels to characters that you can unlock after pulling 16 copies, that the endgame modes would not be balanced around this level of investment. They lied, and to that effect, even the whales with EVERY character at max investment are struggling to clear now.  They've nerfed a character that wasn't particularly strong to begin with under the guise of a "bug fix" in order to avoid having to compensate players for the nerf. This character and the WoD (weapon) that was previously BiS on her were both also rerun right before the nerf, so people have spend lots of money on this combo only to have the interaction between them immediately removed after over a year of the interaction being in the game. They've gutted a system which allows you to gain affinity with your characters, which is essential to view character stories in the game, which means those stories are now functionally impossible to unlock on certain characters with less active playstyles. They previously released a character last month that I bought 4 extra duplicates of specifically because I liked the voice acting the character had. They then bait-and-switched me by removing those voice lines entirely and providing me no compensation for the extra pulls I had spent. This character, which was only released last month, is now also nearly useless in the endgame mode because of the previously mentioned butchering, due to her playstyle not working well with the way they retuned the mode which only adds salt to the wound. I don't know if I plan to change this review back even if they address some of the issues, because the fact they've done all this at once is telling in itself.

items.title: [负面] I don't know where to begin.. Absolutely atrocious...
items.summary:
I don't know where to begin.. Absolutely atrocious update in so many levels. 

1. New D-Tide stat check and difficulty spike is so mindbogglingly stupid, I really have doubts the devs actually play and test the game. It's so bad that even the whales are infuriated with this update. This update practically killed build crafting and funneled the team comp to only select characters, not to mention the insanity of the dmg and HP bloat, like genuinely insane level of bloat. If this is your answer to "+12 AA will not affect future difficulties" then eat a bag of rocks, man. All those apologies and promises, for a small indie team the dev sure acts like a AAA one, in a bad way.

2. Corposant, or rather Horla's WoD interaction with Corposant "bugfix". Right, bugfix. So it's not technically a nerf but bugfix so you can't really compensate players anything like the game told you, so if this is the case then what should I expect for the future if you can just label this nerf as "bugfix" and call it a day. I'm just speaking about this ambiguity, not even talking about the absolute crap that is the nerf itself. This Corpo + Horla's WoD combo has been in the game for so long, I don't believe you only know about this.. "bug" recently. And the fact that this stuff came out AFTER her rerun is downright evil. 

3. Affinity system grind becoming an absolute slog. Don't know what else to say. 

4. Lastly, the way you guys are handling community's feedback, and keep promising stuff, only to deliver this absolute pathetic update before rolling back and conjuring an apology speech again, and again, and again is TIRING. It's becoming a pattern now, and truthfully I don't find any of the apology and promise genuine after the n-th times you guys did it. I always recommend Morimens for the fun build crafting and pretty interesting story, but as it is I don't think I even wanna go back to the game let alone recommending it to people. I'm out.

[负面] English, PT-BR abaixo 
While I loved playing the g...
items.summary:
English, PT-BR abaixo 
While I loved playing the game at first, the current state of the game causes me concern for its future.
- Shop update with the intention to make purchases better ended up increasing the cost of important progression materials, difficulting the economy for new players.
- Nerf disguised as a bugfix for an interaction between character and equipment that existed since the character was launched over a year ago and openly known as BiS for all the community, right after both went through a rerun one after the other, giving it a even more scummy look.
- Changes to affinity systems that demand a insane amount of time investment for a cosmetic that is barely noticeable and could easily be something better with 5 minutes on Photoshop.
- Changes to endgame content that power creeps 90% of the roster with insane damage and HP bloat enemies, while gate keeping pull rewards on difficulties for whales that even they can't easily clear. This changes also reduced the rewards that F2P/starting accounts can get on that mode, severely delaying progression for those accounts as unique materials are gatekept for higher difficulties that need those materials to be cleared.
- Lack of communication for the things above. Ever since the update dropped the devs have been silent ignoring the community criticism about the changes that shouldn't have made past QA.
In any other circumstances I would have song praises for this game. But due to the current state and the fear of what might happen if this and many other issues aren't addressed, I leave this negative review until things get better.

PT-BR:
Embora eu tenha adorado jogar o jogo no início, o estado atual dele me preocupa em relação ao seu futuro.
- Uma atualização da loja, que visava melhorar a experiência de compra, acabou aumentando o custo de materiais importantes para a progressão, prejudicando a economia para novos jogadores.
- Um *nerf* disfarçado de correção de *bug* afetou uma interação entre personagem e equipamento que existia desde o lançamento do personagem, há mais de um ano, e era amplamente reconhecida pela comunidade como a melhor opção (*BiS*). Isso ocorreu logo após ambos terem retornado em *banners* consecutivos, o que tornou a atitude ainda mais questionável.
- Alterações nos sistemas de afinidade exigem um investimento de tempo absurdo para obter um item cosmético quase imperceptível — algo que poderia ter sido facilmente criado em 5 minutos no Photoshop.
- Mudanças no conteúdo de *endgame* tornaram obsoletos 90% dos personagens do elenco devido a inimigos com dano excessivo e vida inflada, ao mesmo tempo em que restringiram as recompensas de invocação a níveis de dificuldade tão elevados que nem mesmo os *whales* (jogadores que gastam muito dinheiro) conseguem superar facilmente. Essas mudanças também reduziram as recompensas acessíveis a jogadores *F2P* (que não gastam dinheiro) e contas iniciantes, atrasando drasticamente a progressão, já que materiais exclusivos ficam restritos a dificuldades elevadas que, ironicamente, exigem justamente esses materiais para serem vencidas.
- Falta de comunicação sobre os pontos mencionados. Desde a atualização, os desenvolvedores mantêm silêncio, ignorando as críticas da comunidade a respeito de mudanças que jamais deveriam ter passado pelo controle de qualidade (*QA*).
Em qualquer outra situação, eu estaria elogiando muito este jogo. No entanto, devido ao estado atual e ao receio do que pode acontecer se esses e outros problemas não forem resolvidos, deixo esta avaliação negativa até que a situação melhore.

items.title: [负面] I want to start by saying this is by far one of th...
items.summary:
I want to start by saying this is by far one of the best games I've played in terms of gameplay, and I specifically liked one gamemode that heavily incentivized team creativity.

That gamemode, has just been utterly destroyed to the core. The easiest difficulty compared to the second easiest has a difference of 10x HP which makes just thinking about playing the game a slog. Previously we had 5 Difficulties and now they've been compressed into 2, with it being arguably harder, including the really bad gimmicks implemented on the final boss. This also came with 2 higher difficulties to appease the whales, which changed absolutely nothing because its just about 9 times the HP of the second easiest difficulty. We were also given the ability to use revives, which we previously couldn't, and it was stated that this would not change the difficulty. And it absolutely did.

This has also come with some questionable changes done to units, all under the guise of a "bug fix", and such mechanics were stablished for long gone (and for the most recent, since release, more than a year ago). What makes it even more dubious is the fact that the unit and the weapon interaction that were changed had just reran back to back, with some people spending tons to maximize this BiS combination.

Its been less than 3 days with no response, which would be fair if the gamemode change wasn't as monumental as it was, making many players uninvested to even want to touch it anymore. 

Back when I joined, there was a very clear future that seemed promising to me. Now? I wouldn't be surprised if it were to be announced to EoS.

Lastly, as just my tiny teensie bit of fustration with the changes, 

"Unplayable" doesn't begin to describe this update, this game rewards pure whaling and nothing else, I am beyond convinced at this point. After waiting hours and hours for the dtide, having to do change my schedule just to fit in my very thin slice of time to play this rotation, attempting hard mode somehow felt even worse than I had thought possible. My team was superior, my relics were superior, my play was superior, and I lost. I don't see a reason to continue engaging in an activity where what is within my control is overwhelmingly outweighed by what is not.

I am done with D-Tide, and you won't get a fond farewell. This rotation is infected to its roots with a degenerative disease that grows stronger over time but stops short of killing its host. Alert 5 used to have a competitive spirit at its heart, this has been transplanted and replaced with an artificial organ that feeds numbers and numbers from fodder mobs that rips appart teams over the pretense of "making the game better". The enviroment we fostered has trapped us all like this in a vicious cycle, and escaping it requires acceptance of the harshest reality we all scramble to explain away, that none of the countless straining efforts we put ourselves through to give feedback will ever amount to one single shining glimmer of a response. I would make this the end, but Arc 2 is still ongoing, and I would never leave so many great friends out dry, so I'll suffer through a few more rotations for them.

One last thing before I leave you all to react with disdain, ridicule, and self-righteous ferver, before you do everything in your power to minimize my words and thoughts, box them up and shove them to some cobwebbed corner of your memory, and hope they disappear forever as a stain on your finite time ground to dust. From this moment on, none of your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gimmicks matter to me. The foulest number bloats, fervor, full immunity, shield ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, with intent to make the game "fun" will calmly settle at the earth before my feet, and the dissolute like a warm summer breeze. This game is less than anything conceivable, while I carry on, brimming with joy distilled from detachment.

items.title: [负面] I absolutely love Morimens, and a few months ago I...
items.summary:
I absolutely love Morimens, and a few months ago I would undoubtedly give the game a positive review. Infact, if the general issues with the games are resolved I will swap my review to positive right away. However, a recent change in management has brought with it a myriad of problems. Instead of the specifics of every horrible patch, I will explain the general trend. In short, the game has been shifting away from openly communicating with and rewarding its community by introducing baffling decision after baffling decision that is causing the most extreme alienation of the player base to date. 

Historically, the developers have been open to feedback and open in discussing their plans. However, lately the communication has been abysmal, with blatant lies regarding viability of certain units/teams and abrupt changes to mechanics right after players have invested large amounts of resources just to learn all their money spent has been rendered essentially worthless in endgame content.

Without delving into the mountain of issues that have been building up patch after patch, it is clear to everyone that the major problem is not just the changes themselves, but the way the developers announce a change, backtrack on the change within a day, THEN BACKTRACK ON THE BACKTRACKING! There is no transparency as to why health numbers are massively inflated by 10x what was promised, or why the new affinity rework is extremely time consuming and unrewarding, or why a known interaction in the game was nerfed after 1.5 years, specifically RIGHT after both the Unit and Wheel involved in the interaction ran FOR MULTIPLE WEEKS!

Everyone understands that a game needs to make money to succeed, and that money must come from somewhere. The game already requires 15(!!) copies to max out a unit, but most content use to be clearable by a dedicated and creative player with the free resources provided (though this requires a lot of knowledge of the meta, since investing too much in the wrong units can brick your account, which is a whole nother issue...). Even still, people do not have an issue with all the ways the game tries to make money, and people understand there is a lot of content designed for whales. Even changes such as buffing +12 units is not something universally disliked. But at the end of the day, everything requires transparency. If you claim to listen to community feedback, why would you lie to their face about thoroughly testing the new changes to endgame content? They claimed to have tested poison and counter on the new mode, when the cap for poison and counter is less than 1/100th of the boss' health!

There is still a lot of good! The game has been great for over 2 years and has built an amazing foundation that tests creativity in teambuilding and gameplay. However, everything that has occurred in the last few months have been a sign that new management does not care about openness, but instead just about squeezing every cent out of player's investment just to pivot with no warning to force everyone to once again open their wallet. I sincerely wish for nothing but the best from this game, but it is mindboggling just how many times the developers have shot themselves in the foot for no reason other than greed. I hope that the people involved in making these decisions listen to the community and reflect on why everyone is angry, and understand that this new business model cannot last.

items.title: [负面] This may unironically be a top 3 worst patches a g...
items.summary:
This may unironically be a top 3 worst patches a gacha has ever made that didn't directly go after pull rates or mass nerf characters. I don't particularly care if it's dev greed, investor greed, "helpful suggestions" from their Japanses partners, or Light's literal brain parasites when it comes to poor game balance philosophy, because the fact this happened to this extent means I really can never recommend this game again.

- Made the already most whale-heavy equipment (covenants) more expensive by creating a system where you now must make a unique set for every character to get their full stats
- Nerfed affinity gain while adding a prohibitively overcosted item to extend further. (couldn't just let people have the pulls from raising affinity, I guess?)
- Made the standard currency shop far more expensive
- Hideous amounts of stat bloat in both story and repeatable content
- """Bugfixed""" an interaction that had existed for over a year, nerfing a character in the process (the character had rerun a matter of weeks prior, and the equipment they interacted with is running *now* and had been running for 2 weeks prior to the bugfix, so it was clearly timed to get pulls before nerfing it. The character isn't even particularly strong. this is the third time they've done this under the guise of a bugfix.
- Probably the most abrasively designed boss the game has ever seen
- Ruined the one gamemode for low/mid-investment players to come around and play semifrequently, making it prohibitively difficult, far too overbearingly scaled between difficulty levels (Minor team improvements matter in basically no content now) and balanced the higher tiers around E3+12 characters (YOU HAVE TO PULL SIXTEEN COPIES OF A CHARACTER TO GET THEIR +12 TALENT) and even then 80% of characters straight up feel unviable in a game with ~60 characters where you need 19-20 to get a clear, and 39-40 to max out potential gains in this mode. There is no middle investment anymore.
- Also there's frequent lag spikes now
- I am almost certainly missing other issues.

Shame that a game where you used to be able to get by by playing exceptionally well has added such nasty stat checks.

Unironically the entire patch could be rolled back, I wouldn't even cry over losing the relatively good (Normal mode is good, holy god the stat bloat in hard) story chapter or losing the pulls on the latest banners. it's that bad. In fact, it's SO bad that I'm not sure I'd feel comfortable spending money on it again unless they went further than rolling it back. the fact they even tried this, even if it got fully rolled back with an apology, dissuades investing in anything. Why would I spend money if half of the roster becomes outright unplayable for the primary content overnight? If interactions can get changed over a year after they occur *in the middle of a rerun banner*? if fights now take *sixty turns*? 

And how long until they do it again if it goes through, or try it in some different way if they do roll it mostly back?
